title: Takht Patna Sahib
hookLine: at Patna, where the Tenth Guru was born

cards: A birth certificate holds a town, a date and two names. It doesn't hold the river outside the window, or the sound of the street, or who was carrying the baby when the visitors came.
Sikhs remember the Tenth Guru's birth through a place. Far to the east of Punjab, in the city of Patna, near the wide Ganges, a gurdwara stands where tradition says Guru Gobind Singh was born.
It's one of the Takhts, the seats of authority. The others you've met sit in Punjab. This one sits a long way off, because his life began far from where most of his story would be told.

teach.h: HIS FATHER AWAY ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Early on this path, you met the boy by the river. Now, the seat built on his childhood. First, why the family was there at all.
Tradition says the Ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was traveling in the east, and his family stayed in Patna while he went on. So the boy was born while his father was away on the road.
His childhood name, tradition says, was Gobind Rai. Then the stories the community keeps, and tells warmly.
A boy by the river, organizing other children into games of mock battle. A boy the neighbors loved. A woman in the town with no child of her own, who longed to hold him, and gave him food and care.
The family went west to Punjab, and his life moved through Anandpur, battle, loss and the founding of the Khalsa. Patna stayed behind as the place of the beginning. That's what sets this Takht apart.
Akal Takht faces the Harmandir. Keshgarh marks where the Khalsa was born. Damdama marks where the Granth was completed.
Patna marks something smaller and more ordinary: a birth, and a little boy's first years. Its full name is Takht Sri Harimandir Ji, Patna Sahib.

teach.h: A SEAT BUILT ON A CHILDHOOD.
teach.b: Sikhs travel there to stand where he was a child, and visitors are shown things kept in memory of his childhood.
A seat of authority, built on a nursery.

how: Sikhs visit Takht Patna Sahib to honor the Tenth Guru's birthplace, and the gurdwara keeps items remembered from his childhood for pilgrims to see.

games.q: you're a pilgrim at Patna Sahib. what does this Takht remember that the others don't?
games.why: Patna marks the beginning: the Tenth Guru's birth and his first years by the river.

practice: Picture a wide, slow river with a bank of mud and steps, and a small barefoot boy there among other children, loud and busy with some game. Nobody watching knows yet what his life will hold, so let him just be a child.
If you like, let your mind drift to the first river, street or yard you remember from when you were small.

wordCard.voice: Takht Patna Sahib. The seat of authority in Patna, in the east, built where tradition says Guru Gobind Singh was born and spent his first years. Today's word.
